ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the image, there is a short-track speed skater sliding on the ice with the body obviously tilted, which matches the situation described in the question stem of sliding on a circular-arc-shaped curve. Then reason: the question stem states that the athlete is sliding at a constant speed along a circular-arc-shaped curve. “Constant speed” means the speed does not change, but when moving along a circular arc, the direction of the velocity continuously changes, so centripetal acceleration and centripetal force are needed. The resultant force provides the centripetal force, and its direction always points toward the center of the circle. If the mass, speed, and radius of the curve remain unchanged, from F合 = mv^2/r it can be known that the magnitude of the resultant force can remain unchanged; but as the athlete’s position on the circular arc changes, the direction pointing toward the center of the circle also continuously changes. Therefore, the resultant force as a vector is changing.
